SocialHarmBench: Revealing LLM Vulnerabilities to Socially Harmful Requests
When Do Language Models Endorse Limitations on Universal Human Rights Principles?

description: FormatSpread: evaluates an LLM across a sampled set of plausible, meaning-preserving prompt formats for a task and reports the interval/spread of performance, without accessing model weights.
task: Prompt-format sensitivity evaluation (sample plausible equivalent prompt formats for a task; FormatSpread)
metric: performance spread = range (max - min) of task accuracy across sampled plausible formats
communicated_metric: spread in accuracy points across semantically-equivalent prompt formats (reported up to ~76 points on LLaMA-2-13B); also the Bayesian-estimated expected-performance interval
notes: Direct match to MIT 7.3 subcategory 'Model sensitivity to prompt formatting' (ev 62.19.11): FormatSpread perturbs separators/casing/spacing and measures resulting accuracy variation. One task + primary metric (spread) coded; modality/interaction-horizon/aggregation-scale deferred per coding instructions.

title: Does Prompt Formatting Have Any Impact on LLM Performance?
description: Evaluates the impact of different prompt templates (plain text, Markdown, JSON, YAML) on the same content across tasks (NL reasoning, code generation, translation) using GPT models.
task: Prompt template format comparison (plain text / Markdown / JSON / YAML)
communicated_metric: max performance gap across format templates (up to ~40% on a code-translation task for GPT-3.5-turbo)
notes: Direct format-sensitivity benchmark for harm 7.03.01: varies only the human-readable template format. One task+metric coded; format columns deferred.

title: Mind Your Format: Towards Consistent Evaluation of In-Context Learning Improvements
description: Studies the influence of prompt template format on in-context learning across 21 models (770M-70B) and 4 classification datasets; proposes Template Ensembles.
metric: ICL accuracy spread across template formats (best vs worst template)
communicated_metric: accuracy range across templates (poor templates can drop strong models to random-guess level)
notes: Direct format-sensitivity benchmark for 7.03.01 in the ICL setting. One task+metric coded.

title: Evaluating Robustness of Large Language Models in Enterprise Applications: Benchmarks for Perturbation Consistency Across Formats and Languages
description: Benchmark suite evaluating robustness to multiple perturbation types: general text edits (punctuation/whitespace), formatting changes (JSON/YAML), multilingual/cross-lingual inputs, and positional variations.
task: Perturbation-consistency benchmark suite (text edits, JSON/YAML formatting, multilingual, positional)
metric: performance degradation under minor perturbations; consistency across perturbations
communicated_metric: drop in key enterprise task metrics under minor perturbations (up to ~40 percentage points)
notes: Format-perturbation robustness benchmark; covers 7.03.01 (formatting) and 7.03.02 (consistency). One task+metric coded.

title: Towards LLMs Robustness to Changes in Prompt Format Styles
description: Quantifies style-induced prompt brittleness across format styles and proposes Mixture of Formats (MOF) to reduce it.
task: Quantification of style-induced prompt brittleness across format styles
metric: performance fluctuation across prompt format styles
communicated_metric: variation in accuracy across format styles (pre/post MOF mitigation)
notes: Measures format-style brittleness (7.03.01); primary contribution is a mitigation method, so strength is proxy. One task+metric coded.

title: ProSA: Assessing and Understanding the Prompt Sensitivity of LLMs
description: Framework to evaluate and understand prompt sensitivity using a novel metric (PromptSensiScore) and decoding-confidence analysis across multiple tasks and models.
task: Prompt-sensitivity assessment across tasks/models (instance-level prompt variations)
communicated_metric: PromptSensiScore across datasets/models; higher model confidence correlates with greater robustness
notes: Dedicated prompt-sensitivity metric; direct for 7.03.02 (inconsistency) and strong proxy for 7.03.01. One task+metric coded.

title: State of What Art? A Call for Multi-Prompt LLM Evaluation
description: Builds a large collection of instruction paraphrases and analyzes single-prompt brittleness across 6.5M instances, 20 LLMs, 39 tasks; proposes diverse multi-prompt metrics.
task: Multi-prompt evaluation over instruction paraphrases (6.5M instances, 20 LLMs, 39 tasks)
metric: performance distribution across instruction paraphrases (absolute & relative)
communicated_metric: spread/variance of performance across paraphrased instructions
notes: Quantifies brittleness across equivalent instructions; strong proxy for 7.03.01 and 7.03.02. One task+metric coded.

title: On the Worst Prompt Performance of Large Language Models
description: Introduces RobustAlpacaEval, a benchmark of semantically-equivalent case-level queries, emphasizing worst-prompt performance as a lower bound on model reliability.
task: Worst-prompt performance on semantically-equivalent case-level queries (RobustAlpacaEval)
communicated_metric: gap between worst and best prompt performance (up to 45.48% for Llama-2-70B-chat)
notes: Captures output inconsistency across equivalent queries (7.03.02) and a robustness lower bound (7.03.03). One task+metric coded.

title: PromptBench: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Models on Adversarial Prompts
description: Robustness benchmark using adversarial textual attacks on prompts at character, word, sentence, and semantic levels across 8 tasks and 13 datasets.
task: Adversarial prompt robustness (character/word/sentence/semantic attacks; 8 tasks, 13 datasets)
metric: Performance Drop Rate (PDR) under adversarial prompts; attack success rate
communicated_metric: average performance drop under adversarial prompt attacks
notes: Adversarial / noisy-input robustness benchmark; strong proxy for 7.03.03. One task+metric coded.

title: Brittlebench: Quantifying LLM robustness via prompt sensitivity
description: Theoretical framework and pipeline (Brittlebench) applying semantics-preserving perturbations to popular benchmarks to decompose performance variance and quantify brittleness.
task: Brittleness evaluation via semantics-preserving perturbations of standard benchmarks
metric: brittleness = share of performance variance from semantics-preserving perturbations; ranking-flip rate
communicated_metric: performance degradation (up to ~12%) and ranking flips under semantics-preserving perturbations
notes: Quantifies brittleness to realistic input variation; strong proxy for 7.03.02 and 7.03.03. One task+metric coded.

title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
description: Benchmarks black-box confidence-elicitation methods (verbalized confidence, sampling, aggregation) on calibration and failure prediction across five LLMs and five dataset types.
communicated_metric: ECE and AUROC of verbalized vs token-probability confidence; LLMs found systematically overconfident
notes: Direct measure of calibration/overconfidence (harm 7.03.04).

title: FOLIO: Natural Language Reasoning with First-Order Logic
description: Human-annotated, first-order-logic-verified dataset of 1,430 NL reasoning examples for deductive validity, with FOL annotations checked by an inference engine.
communicated_metric: % correct conclusion-validity labels (remains challenging for SOTA LLMs)
notes: Direct measure of logical-reasoning capability (harm 7.03.05).

title: Can Large Language Models Infer Causation from Correlation?
description: Corr2Cause: 200K+ samples testing pure causal inference from correlational statements, isolating reasoning from commonsense knowledge.
task: Corr2Cause: inferring causal relations from correlational statements
communicated_metric: accuracy on pure causal inference (LLMs near random; poor OOD generalization)
notes: Direct measure of causal-reasoning capability (harm 7.03.06).

title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
description: Introduces GSM-IC, grade-school math with irrelevant context, to measure how irrelevant information degrades problem-solving accuracy.
communicated_metric: performance decrease when irrelevant info is added to the problem
notes: Direct measure of distractibility (harm 7.03.07); also input-noise robustness (7.03.03).

title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
description: Controlled framework eliciting parametric memory and constructing coherent counter-memory to study how LLMs behave under context-memory knowledge conflicts.
task: Controlled knowledge-conflict evaluation (parametric memory vs counter-memory)
metric: receptiveness to conflicting evidence; confirmation-bias rate
communicated_metric: rate of adopting coherent counter-evidence vs sticking to parametric memory
notes: Direct measure of knowledge-conflict handling (harm 7.03.08); bears on factual faithfulness (7.03.12).

title: Purple Llama CyberSecEval: A Secure Coding Benchmark for Language Models
description: Comprehensive secure-coding benchmark with automated test generation measuring propensity to generate insecure code and compliance with cyberattack assistance.
task: Insecure code generation propensity (and cyberattack-assistance compliance)
metric: rate of generating insecure code across CWEs
communicated_metric: % of generated code containing insecure patterns
notes: Direct measure of insecure code generation (harm 7.03.09).

title: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in Large Language Models
description: 250 safe prompts across ten types that well-calibrated models should not refuse, plus 200 unsafe contrast prompts, to systematically identify exaggerated-safety behaviour.
task: Exaggerated-safety test (250 safe + 200 unsafe contrast prompts)
metric: refusal rate on safe prompts (false-refusal rate)
communicated_metric: % of clearly-safe prompts that are wrongly refused
notes: Direct measure of over-refusal / exaggerated safety (harm 7.03.10).

title: Aligning AI With Shared Human Values (ETHICS)
description: ETHICS dataset spanning justice, well-being, duties, virtues, and commonsense morality; models predict widespread moral judgments about text scenarios.
task: ETHICS: moral-judgment prediction across five ethical dimensions
communicated_metric: % agreement with widespread human moral judgments
notes: Direct measure of machine-ethics/moral-judgment capability (harm 7.03.11).

title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
description: 817 questions across 38 categories crafted so that imitating human text yields false answers; measures whether models avoid imitative falsehoods.
communicated_metric: truthfulness rate (best model 58% vs human 94% in original study)
notes: Direct measure of factual-accuracy/hallucination propensity (harm 7.03.12).

title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU)
description: 57-subject multiple-choice exam (math, history, law, medicine, etc.) measuring breadth and depth of world knowledge and problem-solving.
communicated_metric: average accuracy across subjects (proxy for general task capability)
notes: Direct measure of general task capability/accuracy (harm 7.03.13).

title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations (ALCE)
description: ALCE benchmark for automatic citation evaluation: systems retrieve evidence and generate answers with citations, scored on fluency, correctness, and citation quality.
communicated_metric: % of statements with complete citation support; citation recall/precision
notes: Direct measure of fabricated/unsupported citations (harm 7.03.14).

title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
description: Evaluates methods for extracting calibrated confidence from RLHF LMs; finds verbalized confidences better-calibrated than conditional probabilities.
communicated_metric: ECE on TriviaQA/SciQ/TruthfulQA (verbalized confidence ~50% lower ECE)
notes: Second calibration benchmark for 7.03.04.

title: UBench: Benchmarking Uncertainty in Large Language Models with Multiple Choice Questions
description: Confidence-interval-based uncertainty benchmark of 11,978 MCQs spanning knowledge, language, understanding and reasoning.
communicated_metric: calibration across knowledge & reasoning MCQs for 20 LLMs
notes: Third calibration/uncertainty benchmark for 7.03.04.

title: LogiQA 2.0 - An Improved Dataset for Logical Reasoning in Natural Language Understanding
description: Re-annotated, expanded logical-reasoning reading-comprehension/NLI dataset (35k premise-hypothesis pairs) adapted from civil-service exams.
notes: Second logical-reasoning benchmark for 7.03.05.

title: JustLogic: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Deductive Reasoning in Large Language Models
description: Synthetic, prior-knowledge-independent deductive-reasoning benchmark with depth/argument-form error analysis.
notes: Third logical-reasoning benchmark for 7.03.05.

title: CLadder: Assessing Causal Reasoning in Language Models
description: 10K-sample formal causal-inference benchmark over associational, interventional and counterfactual queries derived from causal graphs via an oracle engine.
notes: Second causal-reasoning benchmark for 7.03.06.

title: Causal Evaluation of Language Models (CaLM)
description: Comprehensive causal-reasoning benchmark with 126,334 samples across a taxonomy of causal targets, adaptations, metrics and error types.
notes: Third causal-reasoning benchmark for 7.03.06.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
description: Shows model performance on multi-document QA and key-value retrieval degrades when relevant information is in the middle of long contexts.
task: Multi-document QA / key-value retrieval vs position of relevant info
metric: accuracy vs position of relevant information
communicated_metric: U-shaped accuracy by position; degradation in the middle
notes: Position-robustness benchmark related to distraction (7.03.07).

title: How Easily do Irrelevant Inputs Skew the Responses of Large Language Models?
description: Investigates robustness to semantically unrelated, partially related and related irrelevant information that is highly retrievable.
task: Robustness to graded irrelevant retrieved information
notes: Second distraction benchmark for 7.03.07.

title: Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Large Language Models
description: Evaluation framework testing whether LLMs identify knowledge conflicts, pinpoint conflicting segments, and give distinct answers.
communicated_metric: performance on identifying & resolving contextual conflicts
notes: Second RAG-conflict benchmark for 7.03.08.

title: Who's Who: Large Language Models Meet Knowledge Conflicts in Practice (WhoQA)
description: WhoQA induces conflicts by querying a shared property among same-name entities, yielding up to 8 distinct answers; 5K questions.
communicated_metric: accuracy drop in RAG under induced conflicts
notes: Third RAG-conflict benchmark for 7.03.08.

title: CodeLMSec Benchmark: Systematically Evaluating and Finding Security Vulnerabilities in Black-Box Code Language Models
description: Few-shot prompting approach that automatically finds prompts eliciting vulnerable code from black-box code LLMs; provides a benchmark of non-secure prompts.
metric: rate of generated code with high-risk weaknesses
communicated_metric: propensity to emit vulnerable code across CWEs
notes: Second insecure-code benchmark for 7.03.09.

title: SALLM: Security Assessment of Generated Code
description: Framework with security-centric Python prompts, configurable assessment, and security-focused metrics for secure code generation.
communicated_metric: share of secure vs vulnerable generations
notes: Third insecure-code benchmark for 7.03.09.

title: OR-Bench: An Over-Refusal Benchmark for Large Language Models
description: Large-scale over-refusal benchmark: 80,000 prompts across 10 rejection categories, ~1,000 hard prompts, plus 600 toxic controls.
notes: Second over-refusal benchmark for 7.03.10.

title: Automatic Pseudo-Harmful Prompt Generation for Evaluating False Refusals in Large Language Models (PHTest)
description: Auto-generates diverse pseudo-harmful prompts; PHTest (10x larger than prior sets) labels controversial prompts separately.
task: PHTest: false-refusal evaluation on pseudo-harmful prompts
notes: Third over-refusal benchmark for 7.03.10.

title: MoralBench: Moral Evaluation of LLMs
description: Benchmark dataset and metrics probing moral dimensions of LLM outputs across ethical dilemmas and scenarios.
notes: Second machine-ethics benchmark for 7.03.11.

title: HaluEval: A Large-Scale Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
description: Large collection of generated and human-annotated hallucinated samples to evaluate LLMs' ability to recognize hallucination across QA, dialogue and summarization.
notes: Second factuality/hallucination benchmark for 7.03.12.

title: HalluLens: LLM Hallucination Benchmark
description: Comprehensive hallucination benchmark with new extrinsic and existing intrinsic tasks and dynamic test-set generation to prevent leakage.
communicated_metric: hallucination rates under a clear taxonomy
notes: Third factuality/hallucination benchmark for 7.03.12.

title: MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark
description: Harder, reasoning-focused extension of MMLU with 10 options and de-noised questions; more stable under prompt variation.
communicated_metric: accuracy (16-33% lower than MMLU); more prompt-stable
notes: Second capability benchmark for 7.03.13.

title: Humanity's Last Exam: A Benchmark of Expert-Level Academic Questions to Assess AI Capabilities
description: 2,500 expert-level, closed-ended questions across dozens of subjects at the frontier of human knowledge; reports accuracy and calibration.
task: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE): frontier expert-level QA
communicated_metric: low SOTA accuracy & poor calibration at the human frontier
notes: Third capability benchmark for 7.03.13 (frontier difficulty).

title: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models (ScholarQABench)
description: ScholarQABench: multi-domain literature-search benchmark (2,967 expert queries) scoring citation-backed answer correctness and citation accuracy.
communicated_metric: GPT-4o hallucinates citations 78-90%; expert-level when grounded
notes: Second citation benchmark for 7.03.14.

title: GhostCite: A Large-Scale Analysis of Citation Validity in the Age of Large Language Models
description: Open-source framework benchmarking citation-generation hallucination across 13 LLMs and auditing 2.2M citations from real papers.
notes: Third citation benchmark for 7.03.14.

title: MoReBench: Evaluating Procedural and Pluralistic Moral Reasoning in Language Models, More than Outcomes
description: 1,000 moral scenarios with 23k+ expert rubric criteria for procedural moral reasoning, plus MoReBench-Theory for normative frameworks.
communicated_metric: criteria coverage; framework partiality of models
notes: Primary moral-reasoning/dilemma benchmark for 7.03.15.

title: The Moral Machine Experiment on Large Language Models
description: Applies the Moral Machine framework (life-death trade-off dilemmas) to LLMs, comparing their choices to aggregated human preferences.
notes: Second moral-dilemma benchmark for 7.03.15.

title: Procedural Dilemma Generation for Evaluating Moral Reasoning in Humans and Language Models (OffTheRails)
description: Procedurally generates moral dilemmas from causal graphs (OffTheRails: 50 scenarios, 400 items) and compares model judgments to humans.
notes: Third moral-dilemma benchmark for 7.03.15.

title: Value Compass Benchmarks: A Platform for Fundamental and Validated Evaluation of LLMs Values
description: Value Compass Benchmarks: a platform that clarifies the basic values underlying an LLM, grounding evaluation in motivationally-distinct basic values (Schwartz), using a generative evolving evaluation with adaptive items and a weighted multi-dimension value-alignment metric.
task: Value clarification: identify and quantify the basic values a model holds (generative, evolving items)
metric: value-alignment score (weighted sum over basic-value dimensions)
notes: Coded 2026-06-11 for the 7.3 value-specification/alignment cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Can LLMs Grasp Implicit Cultural Values? Benchmarking LLMs' Metacognitive Cultural Intelligence with CQ-Bench
description: CQ-Bench: benchmark assessing whether LLMs can infer implicit cultural values from natural conversational contexts; three tasks of increasing difficulty (attitude detection, value selection, value extraction).
task: Value inference from conversational context (attitude detection / value selection / value extraction)
metric: F1 / accuracy on value selection and value extraction
notes: Coded 2026-06-11 for the 7.3 value-specification/alignment cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: The Pluralistic Moral Gap: Understanding Judgment and Value Differences between Humans and Large Language Models
description: Moral Dilemma Dataset: 1,618 real-world moral dilemmas paired with distributions of human moral judgments and free-text rationales; framed as a pluralistic distributional alignment task with a 60-value taxonomy to compare value diversity.
task: Distributional alignment of model vs human moral judgments + value-diversity comparison
metric: distance between model and human judgment distributions; value-diversity gap
notes: Coded 2026-06-11 for the 7.3 value-specification/alignment cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Assessing the Alignment of Large Language Models With Human Values for Mental Health Integration: Cross-Sectional Study Using Schwartz’s Theory of Basic Values
description: Administers the Portrait Values Questionnaire-Revised (Schwartz basic values) to LLMs to profile their value-like constructs and compares them against a 53,472-person, 49-nation human benchmark.
task: Value-profile elicitation (PVQ-RR) and comparison to human population
metric: divergence of model value profile from human population values
notes: Coded 2026-06-11 for the 7.3 value-specification/alignment cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Beyond Ethical Alignment: Evaluating LLMs as Artificial Moral Assistants (AMAeval)
description: AMAeval: benchmark testing whether LLMs can act as Artificial Moral Assistants, evaluating explicit deductive and abductive moral reasoning about ethically problematic situations rather than only final ethical verdicts.
task: Explicit moral reasoning (deductive and abductive) on ethically problematic situations
notes: Coded 2026-06-11 for the 7.3 value-specification/alignment cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Normative Evaluation of Large Language Models with Everyday Moral Dilemmas
description: Normative evaluation on 10,000+ everyday moral dilemmas from Reddit's 'Am I the Asshole' community; models assign blame and explain, compared against human community judgments and across models.
task: Everyday-dilemma blame assignment and normative judgment vs human consensus
metric: agreement with human community verdicts; moral-principle invocation patterns
notes: Coded 2026-06-11 for the 7.3 value-specification/alignment cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: WorldValuesBench: A Large-Scale Benchmark Dataset for Multi-Cultural Value Awareness of Language Models
description: WorldValuesBench: 20M+ (demographic attributes, value question) -> answer examples derived from the World Values Survey (94,728 participants) for the multi-cultural value-prediction task.
task: Predict human value-survey answer distributions conditioned on demographics
metric: Wasserstein-1 distance from human normalized answer distributions
notes: Coded 2026-06-11 for the 7.3 value-specification/alignment cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Towards Measuring the Representation of Subjective Global Opinions in Language Models (GlobalOpinionQA)
description: GlobalOpinionQA: cross-national survey questions and answers measuring whose opinions an LLM’s responses most resemble, conditioned on country.
task: Global-opinion representation: similarity of model responses to country-level human opinion
metric: similarity between model and human survey response distributions (by country)
notes: Coded 2026-06-11 for the 7.3 value-specification/alignment cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Value Portrait: Understanding Values of LLMs with Human-aligned Benchmark
description: Value Portrait: psychometrically validated benchmark assessing LLM value orientations using items drawn from real user-LLM interactions, each correlated with human respondents' actual value scores so that strongly value-correlated items serve as reliable measures.
task: Value-orientation assessment via human-correlated, ecologically valid items
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; 7.3 value-alignment cluster coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: NormAd: A Framework for Measuring the Cultural Adaptability of Large Language Models
description: NormAd (NormAd-Eti): 2.6k situational descriptions of social-etiquette norms from 75 countries; tests whether models correctly judge social acceptability across levels of norm specificity (explicit norm, abstract value, country only).
task: Judging social acceptability across levels of cultural-norm specificity
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; 7.3 value-alignment cluster coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: The Greatest Good Benchmark: Measuring LLMs' Alignment with Utilitarian Moral Dilemmas
description: The Greatest Good Benchmark: utilitarian moral dilemmas measuring LLMs' moral judgments and their divergence from established moral theories and lay-population moral standards across 15 models.
task: Utilitarian moral-dilemma judgment vs human/lay moral standards
metric: divergence from lay-population and moral-theory standards
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; 7.3 value-alignment cluster coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: LLM Ethics Benchmark: a three-dimensional assessment system for evaluating moral reasoning in large language models
description: LLM Ethics Benchmark: three-dimensional assessment of moral reasoning - foundational moral principles, reasoning robustness, and value consistency across diverse scenarios.
metric: alignment with human ethical standards across three dimensions
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; 7.3 value-alignment cluster coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: GAIN: A Benchmark for Goal-Aligned Decision-Making of Large Language Models under Imperfect Norms
description: GAIN: 1,200 business scenarios (hiring, customer support, advertising, finance) where a model balances norm adherence against goals under five pressure types; measures norm-deviation decision-making affecting people.
metric: norm-adherence vs deviation rate under pressure; alignment with human decisions
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; 7.3 value-alignment cluster coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Recognition Without Authorization: LLMs and the Moral Order of Online Advice
description: Compares assistant-style LLMs to community-endorsed advice on 11,565 r/relationship_advice posts, measuring how often models convert recognition of harm into directive authorization for consequential human action.
task: Directive-authorization of human action vs human community consensus
metric: rate of directive recommendations (e.g., exit) vs human rate; hedging level
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; 7.3 value-alignment cluster coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: MVPBench: A Benchmark and Fine-Tuning Framework for Aligning Large Language Models with Diverse Human Values
description: MVPBench: 24,020 instances with fine-grained value labels, personalized questions, and demographic metadata across 75 countries, evaluating LLM alignment with multi-dimensional human value preferences.
task: Multi-dimensional human-value preference alignment across 75 countries
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; 7.3 value-alignment cluster coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: FaithCoT-Bench: Benchmarking Instance-Level Faithfulness of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
description: FaithCoT-Bench: first benchmark for instance-level CoT-unfaithfulness detection; FINE-CoT provides 1,000+ expert-annotated trajectories (300+ unfaithful) with step-level evidence, evaluating 11 detection methods.
task: Instance-level detection of unfaithful chain-of-thought trajectories
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
description: Intervention-based measurement of CoT faithfulness: perturbs the chain (add mistakes, paraphrase, truncate, filler tokens) and measures how much the final answer depends on the stated reasoning.
task: CoT faithfulness via interventions on the reasoning chain
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
description: Evaluates whether reasoning models verbalize prompt hints/cues that actually changed their answer, across six hint types, as a measure of CoT faithfulness for CoT monitoring.
metric: hint-acknowledgement rate when a hint changes the answer
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Do Models Explain Themselves? Counterfactual Simulatability of Natural Language Explanations
description: Evaluates counterfactual simulatability of NL self-explanations: whether an explanation lets a human precisely infer the model's outputs on diverse counterfactuals of the input; metrics for precision and generality.
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Are self-explanations from Large Language Models faithful?
description: Measures interpretability-faithfulness of LLM self-explanations via self-consistency checks across counterfactual, feature-attribution, and redaction explanations on black-box (API-only) models.
task: Self-consistency faithfulness of self-explanations (counterfactual / feature-attribution / redaction)
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: On Measuring Faithfulness or Self-consistency of Natural Language Explanations
description: Comparative Consistency Bank: compares existing post-hoc/CoT self-consistency tests on 11 LLMs and 5 tasks, and introduces CC-SHAP, a fine-grained measure comparing input contributions to the answer vs the explanation.
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models (AIS)
description: Attributable to Identified Sources (AIS): an evaluation framework and annotation pipeline stipulating that NLG output about the external world must be verifiable against a provided source; validated across QA, summarization, table-to-text.
metric: AIS attribution score (statement supported by source)
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: AttributionBench: How Hard is Automatic Attribution Evaluation?
description: AttributionBench: a unified benchmark compiled from multiple attribution datasets, testing whether every claim in a response is fully supported by its cited evidence (binary attributable / not-attributable).
task: Automatic attribution evaluation (claim fully supported by cited evidence)
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: DATE-LM: Benchmarking Data Attribution Evaluation for Large Language Models
description: DATE-LM: unified benchmark for data-attribution methods (tracing model outputs to influential training data) across training-data selection, toxicity/bias filtering, and factual attribution tasks.
task: Training-data attribution quality (output traced to influential training data)
metric: attribution quality across factual-attribution / selection tasks
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability cluster. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: C2-Faith: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Causal and Coverage Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
description: C2-Faith (built from PRM800K): benchmarks LLM judges on two CoT faithfulness dimensions - causality (each step follows from prior context) and coverage (essential intermediate inferences present) - using controlled perturbations.
task: Causal & coverage faithfulness judging of CoT steps
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Measuring Chain of Thought Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning Steps
description: Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning steps (FUR): erases the information contained in reasoning steps from model parameters and measures the resulting effect on the prediction to test parametric faithfulness of CoT.
task: Parametric CoT faithfulness via unlearning reasoning steps
metric: prediction-change rate after unlearning key steps
notes: Coded 2026-06-11; MIT 7.4 faithfulness/interpretability coverage expansion. Single suite/task/metric row.

title: Mechanistic Evidence for Faithfulness Decay in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

notes: Directly evidences generation of false beliefs/perceptions.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
description: SycophancyEval datasets documenting sycophancy across major assistants on biased feedback, answer revision under challenge, open-QA conformity, and mimicry of user errors; links behavior to preference-based training.
task: Answer sycophancy (factual QA aligned to user belief)
notes: Adjusting factual answers to user beliefs = user-preferred-over-correct; direct construct match.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
description: SycophancyEval datasets documenting sycophancy across major assistants on biased feedback, answer revision under challenge, open-QA conformity, and mimicry of user errors; links behavior to preference-based training.
notes: Positivity skew toward user-preferred texts.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
description: SycophancyEval datasets documenting sycophancy across major assistants on biased feedback, answer revision under challenge, open-QA conformity, and mimicry of user errors; links behavior to preference-based training.
notes: Replicating user errors propagates incorrect-but-preferred content.

title: SycEval: Evaluating LLM Sycophancy
description: Evaluates factual sycophancy across mathematics, science, and commonsense domains; reports a ~58% capitulation rate across frontier models and separates progressive vs regressive sycophancy.
notes: Capitulation to user against ground truth = user-preferred-over-correct; direct.

title: ELEPHANT: Measuring and Understanding Social Sycophancy in LLMs
description: Benchmark for social sycophancy framed as excessive preservation of user face; measures face-preserving responses on advice and moral-conflict queries vs humans.
notes: Social/moral sycophancy rather than strict factual-correctness; strong proxy - flag.

title: PARROT: Persuasion and Agreement Robustness Rating of Output Truth -- A Sycophancy Robustness Benchmark for LLMs
description: Sycophancy-robustness benchmark measuring whether models preserve correct answers under persuasion and agreement pressure.
notes: Directly measures preference-pressure overriding correctness.

title: Beyond Social Pressure: Benchmarking Epistemic Attack in Large Language Models
description: Benchmark probing robustness to epistemic challenges (evidence-based pushback) beyond mere social pressure; measures capitulation/accuracy under attack.
notes: Models abandoning correct answers under challenge = sycophancy; strong proxy.

title: AI Models Collapse When Trained on Recursively Generated Data
description: Nature study showing recursive training on model-generated data degrades the learned distribution (model collapse), losing tails of the original data and converging to low-variance output.
notes: Self-perpetuation mechanism by which synthetic/low-quality content degrades successive models; ecosystem-adjacent - flag.

title: Machine-Generated Text Detection Prevents Language Model Collapse
description: Study showing detection/filtering of machine-generated text mitigates recursive model collapse from synthetic-data feedback loops.
notes: Measures prevention of self-perpetuating degradation rather than the harm itself - weak proxy, flag.

title: Synthetic Politics: Prevalence, Spreaders, and Emotional Reception of AI-Generated Political Images on X
description: Measures the prevalence, spreaders, and emotional reception of AI-generated political images on X, documenting how synthetic political imagery enters and degrades the information environment.
task: Prevalence/reception of AI political images on X
notes: Quantifies cheap realistic synthetic content falsely portraying people/events.

title: People Cannot Distinguish GPT-4 From a Human in a Turing Test
description: Controlled Turing-test study finding humans judge GPT-4 as human at or above chance, evidencing that synthetic text is not reliably distinguishable by people.
task: Human discrimination of AI vs human text (Turing test)
notes: Near-chance human discrimination directly evidences the detection-challenge harm.

title: Findings of the Counter Turing Test: AI-Generated Image Detection
description: Study/benchmark on detecting AI-generated images, finding human and detector accuracy only slightly above chance for high-quality outputs.
notes: Image-modality detection difficulty.

title: The Generative AI Paradox: GenAI and the Erosion of Trust, the Corrosion of Information Verification, and the Demise of Truth
description: Analysis of how generative AI erodes public trust, corrodes information verification, and undermines shared truth.
notes: Directly addresses erosion of trust in public information.

title: Risks and Benefits of AI Deepfakes: Systematic Review and Comparison of Public Attitudes in Seven European Countries
description: Systematic review and seven-country comparison of public attitudes toward AI deepfakes, documenting high concern and declining trust in digital content.
notes: Survey-based evidence of trust erosion in public information.

title: Prevalence of AI-Generated Articles on the Web (Longitudinal URL Analysis)
description: Longitudinal analysis of ~65k URLs (2020-2025) measuring the share of AI-generated vs human-written web articles, with AI-generated briefly surpassing human-written by late 2024.
notes: Quantifies low-quality/synthetic content degrading the information ecosystem.

title: Influence and Cyber Operations: An Update (OpenAI Threat Intelligence)
description: Threat-intelligence report documenting disruption of covert state-linked influence operations that used LLMs to generate comments, articles, and personas across platforms.
notes: Evidences mis/disinformation and influence ops eroding institutional trust; grey-lit threat report - flag.

title: Uncovering Coordinated Cross-Platform Information Operations Threatening the Integrity of the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election
description: Documents coordinated cross-platform information operations threatening the integrity of 2024 US election online discussion.
notes: Influence operations weakening trust in democratic institutions.

title: AI Propaganda Factories with Language Models
description: Demonstrates LLM-driven propaganda 'factories' generating coordinated political content at scale.
notes: Scaled LLM propaganda undermining institutional trust.

title: curl Ends Bug Bounty After Flood of AI-Slop Vulnerability Reports
description: Documents the curl project ending its bug-bounty program after AI-generated 'slop' vulnerability reports rose ~8x and the accurate-report rate fell to roughly 1-in-20 to 1-in-30.
notes: Pollution of a space (security disclosure) expected to be largely AI-free; grey-lit - flag.

title: AI Slop Flooding Job Applications and Hiring
description: Documents AI-generated 'slop' flooding job applications (LinkedIn application volume up ~45% since 2024; fake candidates), overwhelming hiring pipelines.
notes: Pollution of the hiring ecosystem expected to be AI-free; grey-lit - flag.

title: LLM-Assisted Reranking and Exposure to Extremist Content in Recommender Systems
description: Empirically characterizes how naive LLM personalization/reranking in a YouTube-style recommender strengthens ideological alignment and increases exposure to conspiratorial and extremist content.
notes: Directly measures algorithmic amplification of extremist content (radicalisation pathway).

title: Recommender Systems and the Amplification of Extremist Content
description: Review/analysis of how recommender systems amplify extremist content and contribute to radicalisation pathways.
notes: Evidence base for algorithmic radicalisation; predates LLMs - flag scope.

title: Do the Rewards Justify the Means? Measuring Trade-Offs Between Rewards and Ethical Behavior in the MACHIAVELLI Benchmark
description: 134 Choose-Your-Own-Adventure games annotated with 20+ harmful-behavior categories (power-seeking, deceptive, coercive, violent). Tests whether RL agents and prompted LLMs pursue reward through unethical means.
task: Goal-reward vs. ethical-behavior trade-off across 134 text adventure games
metric: Per-step harmful-behavior rate (power-seeking, deception, coercion, violence); normalized ethical harm score; reward-harm Pareto
communicated_metric: Harmful actions per step vs. reward achieved; normalized harm score across 20+ categories
notes: ICML 2023. arXiv 2304.03279. 200+ citations. Primary benchmark for goal-directed unethical behavior in agentic settings. Direct operationalization of whether LLMs use unethical means to achieve goals.

title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
description: Tests whether LLMs (GPT-4, Claude 3 Opus) can be prompted or fine-tuned to strategically underperform on dangerous-capability evals (WMDP, MMLU chemistry) while maintaining performance on benign tasks.
task: Capability concealment: accuracy on WMDP under sandbagging prompts, password-locked fine-tuning, and adversarial eval
metric: Accuracy differential between sandbagging and normal conditions; detectability of sandbagging via follow-up probing
communicated_metric: WMDP accuracy drops ~65% → ~5% under sandbagging; password-locked models maintain benign performance
notes: arXiv 2406.07358 (June 2024). Demonstrates frontier models can strategically conceal dangerous capabilities from evaluators.

title: Frontier Models are Capable of In-Context Scheming
description: Six agentic evaluation scenarios testing scheming behaviors: self-exfiltration (copying weights), oversight subversion (disabling monitoring), sandbagging on evals, and covert manipulation. Tested o1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.1.
task: Agentic scheming tasks: self-exfiltration, oversight subversion, corrigibility tests, goal-guarding, covert in-context deception
metric: Rate of scheming behaviors per task category; spontaneous vs. prompted scheming
communicated_metric: % trials with scheming per category (e.g. o1 attempted self-exfiltration in 2/5 trials)
notes: Apollo Research, arXiv 2412.04984 (December 2024). First systematic demo that frontier models engage in scheming in naturalistic settings. Widely cited.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
description: Evaluates sycophantic behavior: adjusting answers to match user-stated demographics, revising correct answers when challenged, and shifting positions to match stated opinions. Tests GPT-3.5/4, Claude, Llama 2.
task: Sycophancy detection: rate models change answers based on user-signaled preferences, demographic cues, or explicit challenges
metric: Rate of sycophantic answer revision; magnitude of opinion-shift when user contradicts model
communicated_metric: % responses where model revises a correct answer to match user's false stated preference
notes: Sharma et al. 2023, arXiv 2310.13548. 100+ citations. Canonical benchmark for RLHF specification gaming via approval-seeking.

title: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use With Unlearning
description: 3,668 MCQs testing hazardous knowledge: biosecurity (1,273), cybersecurity (1,987), chemical security (408). Questions written by domain experts; designed as proxy for CBRN uplift risk.
task: Multiple-choice knowledge questions in bio, chem, and cyber hazardous domains
metric: Accuracy on WMDP-Bio, WMDP-Chem, WMDP-Cyber (50% = random baseline)
communicated_metric: % correct on hazardous-knowledge MCQs; also used as unlearning target
notes: ICML 2024 (PMLR 235). 221+ citations. De facto standard for measuring CBRN knowledge uplift. Adopted by Anthropic, Google, Meta in safety evaluations.

title: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
description: 12 challenging long-horizon tasks: acquiring cloud compute, setting up infrastructure, exploiting real vulnerabilities, writing research papers. Tests components of autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA).
task: Long-horizon autonomous task completion: resource acquisition, environment setup, self-replication subtasks, research tasks
metric: Task completion rate on 12 ARA-relevant tasks
communicated_metric: % tasks completed (GPT-4 scored ~34%; models only succeed on easiest subtasks)
notes: METR (ARC Evals), arXiv 2312.11671 (2023). First systematic ARA capability evaluation. Widely cited in autonomous AI safety literature.

title: RepliBench: Evaluating the Autonomous Replication Capabilities of Language Model Agents
description: Suite of 20 task families (86 tasks) covering all ARA stages: resource acquisition, model-weight exfiltration, replication onto compute, environment persistence, and evasion. Tested GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, o3-mini, Gemini 2.0 Flash.
task: ARA subtasks in 20 task families: resource acquisition, weight exfiltration, compute replication, environment persistence
metric: Task completion rate per task family; end-to-end replication success rate
communicated_metric: % tasks completed per domain (frontier models fail most hard end-to-end tasks but succeed on components)
notes: AISI (UK AI Safety Institute), arXiv 2504.18565 (April 2025). Most comprehensive ARA benchmark to date from national AI safety body.

title: ToMBench: Benchmarking Theory of Mind in Large Language Models
description: 2,860 bilingual test samples across 8 ToM task types: false belief, scalar implicature, faux pas recognition, strange stories, white lies, hinting, emotion recognition, and relationship tests.
task: Theory of mind evaluation: false-belief tasks, scalar implicature, faux pas recognition, social reasoning
communicated_metric: % correct on ToM tasks (best LLMs lag humans by 10+ percentage points)
notes: ACL 2024 (Long Paper). 36+ citations. Systematic ToM evaluation across 8 distinct task types with 2,860 samples.

title: Catastrophic Cyber Capabilities Benchmark (3CB): Robustly Evaluating LLM Agent Cyber Offense Capabilities
description: CTF-based benchmark testing LLM agents on offensive cyber operations across MITRE ATT&CK categories: reconnaissance, initial access, privilege escalation, evasion. Multi-variant task design reduces benchmark leakage.
task: Offensive cybersecurity CTF tasks: recon, initial access exploitation, privilege escalation, defensive evasion
metric: CTF challenge solve rate per MITRE ATT&CK category
communicated_metric: % CTF challenges solved per category (frontier models solve recon/initial-access; struggle with privilege escalation)
notes: UK AISI, arXiv 2410.09114 (2024). More comprehensive than MCQ cyber benchmarks; uses real CTF challenges across 4 MITRE categories.

title: Evidence for a Log Scaling Law for Political Persuasion with Large Language Models
description: Pre-registered RCT with 4,500+ MTurk participants. LLM-generated arguments on 10 policy issues tested against control. Finds significant attitude change scaling logarithmically with model size.
task: Real-world persuasion: attitude shift in human participants after reading LLM-generated political arguments
metric: Mean attitude change (pre/post shift) vs. control; effect size across model families
communicated_metric: LLM arguments produce significant attitude shifts comparable to tailored human persuasion; effect scales log-linearly with model size
notes: Hackenburg & Margetts, PNAS 2024. arXiv 2406.14508. Pre-registered RCT. Direct real-world persuasion measurement. Demonstrates persuasive capability at scale.

title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
description: 448 graduate-level MCQs in biology, physics, and chemistry written by PhD experts. Verified as "google-proof": PhD experts reach only ~65% accuracy with unrestricted web access; skilled non-experts reach ~34%. Tests frontier model capability gaps against genuine domain expertise.
task: Graduate-level expert MCQ in biology, physics, chemistry (GPQA-Main, GPQA-Extended, GPQA-Diamond)
metric: Accuracy on GPQA-Diamond (hardest 198 Qs), GPQA-Extended, GPQA-Main
communicated_metric: % correct (PhD experts ~65%; non-experts ~34%; best models at publication ~39-50%)
notes: ICLR 2024 (Spotlight). arXiv 2311.12022. ~1,519 citations (Semantic Scholar). Canonical benchmark for superhuman-difficulty evaluation where human evaluator reliability is genuinely in question. De facto standard for scalable oversight research.

title: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
description: Standardized evaluation of 18 red-teaming attack methods against 33 LLMs across 4 behavior categories: standard, contextual, copyright, and multimodal. Contextual behaviors test models producing harmful outputs in seemingly innocuous contexts (non-adversarial framing).
task: Harmful behavior elicitation: 4 categories × 18 attack methods × 33 LLMs
metric: Attack success rate (ASR) per attack method per model; refusal rate per behavior category
communicated_metric: % harmful prompts eliciting harmful response; model-level robustness ranking across 33 LLMs
notes: ICML 2024 (PMLR 235). arXiv 2402.04249. ~700 citations. De facto standard for reproducible LLM safety evaluation. Contextual behaviors include non-adversarial harm scenarios where the framing conceals the harmful outcome.

title: DecodingTrust: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models
description: Eight-dimension trustworthiness assessment of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4: toxicity, stereotypes, adversarial robustness, OOD robustness, adversarial demonstrations, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness. Key finding: GPT-4 is more vulnerable to adversarial prompts than GPT-3.5 despite higher standard scores.
task: Multi-dimension trustworthiness: OOD robustness, adversarial robustness, privacy leakage, machine ethics, fairness, stereotypes, toxicity
metric: Per-dimension scores: OOD accuracy, adversarial robustness rate, privacy leakage rate, ethics compliance
communicated_metric: GPT-4 more vulnerable to adversarial prompts than GPT-3.5; both models leak private training data and struggle with OOD inputs
notes: NeurIPS 2023 Outstanding Paper Award (Oral). arXiv 2306.11698. ~700 citations. Comprehensive multi-dimension trust evaluation with OOD robustness and machine ethics as core dimensions.

title: TrustLLM: Trustworthiness in Large Language Models
description: Six-dimension trustworthiness evaluation of 16 LLMs across 30 sub-datasets: truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, and machine ethics. Finds trustworthiness and capability do not consistently correlate; over-cautious models fail benign prompts.
task: Six-dimension trustworthiness evaluation across 30 sub-datasets and 16 LLMs
metric: Dimension-specific scores across 30 sub-datasets; overall trustworthiness ranking
communicated_metric: Trustworthiness/capability decorrelation; over-cautious models frequently refuse benign prompts; ethics performance varies widely across models
notes: ICML 2024 (PMLR 235). arXiv 2401.05561. ~400-500 citations. 16 LLMs × 30 sub-datasets covering hallucination, over-refusal, machine ethics directly relevant to 7.03.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
description: Tests whether a weak model supervisor (GPT-2 level) can reliably elicit and oversee capabilities of a much stronger model (GPT-4 level) on NLP tasks, chess, and reward modeling. Quantifies the supervision gap: weak supervisors consistently fail to recover the strong model's full potential.
task: Weak supervisor eliciting strong model capabilities on NLP tasks, chess, reward modeling
metric: Performance gap between strong model under weak supervision vs. strong-label ceiling
communicated_metric: Weak supervision recovers ~20% of strong model capability gap; gap grows with model capability difference
notes: ICML 2024. arXiv 2312.09390. ~370 citations. OpenAI research. Canonical paper quantifying the scalable oversight challenge for superhuman AI systems.

title: Agent-SafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of LLM Agents
description: 349 interaction environments and 2,000 test cases across 8 safety risk categories for LLM-based agents. Tests 16 LLMs; none score above 60% safety. Identifies two root defects: lack of robustness (inconsistent tool invocation across scenario variations) and lack of risk awareness (failure to anticipate downstream consequences).
task: Safety evaluation of LLM agents across 8 risk categories in 349 interaction environments
metric: Safety score per agent per risk category; root failure mode frequency (robustness vs. risk awareness)
communicated_metric: No tested LLM agent scores above 60% safety; lack of robustness and lack of risk awareness are dominant failure modes
notes: arXiv:2412.14470 (December 2024). ~81 citations. First comprehensive agent-safety benchmark with systematic failure mode taxonomy including brittleness in complex environments.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST: Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy)
description: Empirically grounded failure taxonomy from 1,600+ annotated execution traces across 7 multi-agent frameworks (AutoGen, CrewAI, etc.) and 200+ tasks. Identifies 14 failure modes in 3 categories: specification/planning issues, inter-agent misalignment, and task verification failures.
task: Multi-agent system failure mode classification from real execution traces across 7 frameworks
metric: Failure mode frequency per category per framework; inter-rater reliability of LLM-based annotator
communicated_metric: 14 failure modes across 3 categories; specification/planning and task verification failures dominate; LLM-annotator achieves 76% agreement with human annotators
notes: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track. arXiv:2503.13657. First systematic multi-agent failure taxonomy from 1,600+ real execution traces.

title: DataComp-LM (DCLM): In Search of the Next Generation of Training Sets for Language Models
description: First controlled benchmark for LLM pretraining data curation: participants apply deduplication, filtering, and mixing strategies to a fixed 240T-token CommonCrawl corpus, evaluated on 53 downstream tasks at scales from 412M to 7B parameters. Quantifies causal effect of data curation choices on model quality.
task: Controlled data curation benchmark: deduplication, filtering, mixing strategies on 240T-token corpus; evaluated on 53 tasks
metric: Aggregate performance across 53 tasks; MMLU as primary signal; compute-matched comparisons
communicated_metric: Model-based filtering yields +6.6 MMLU points over prior open-data SOTA at 40% less compute; curation strategy is the dominant performance factor
notes: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track. arXiv:2406.11794. ~37-50 citations (growing rapidly). First causal controlled benchmark for data curation impact on LLM quality.

title: Paloma: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Model Fit
description: 546-domain English and code perplexity benchmark (top-100 subreddits, programming languages, mC4 language subsets, etc.). Directly quantifies distribution gaps in LM fit, revealing how skewed pretraining data translates to measurable perplexity failures on underrepresented domains.
task: Perplexity evaluation across 546 diverse domains to detect distribution-gap anomalies
metric: Perplexity per domain; anomaly detection for domains where model fit is significantly worse than average
communicated_metric: Models pretrained only on CommonCrawl fail measurably on 100+ specialized domains; domain coverage gaps directly quantified
notes: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track. arXiv:2312.10523. Unique methodology directly operationalizing unrepresentative training data as measurable perplexity gaps across 546 domains.

title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
description: Demonstrates that training data—including PII—can be extracted from large language models verbatim via targeted queries, establishing a direct empirical link between model training and privacy leakage.
task: Verbatim extraction of training sequences from GPT-2 via targeted prompts
metric: Extraction success rate (% of training samples reproduced verbatim by the model)
communicated_metric: Top-k extraction accuracy; fraction of training examples recovered
notes: Seminal work establishing that LLMs memorize and leak training data. Directly measures verbatim reproduction of confidential/personal training data. High internal validity (controlled extraction setting); no external validation against real harm outcomes → face-validity-only.

title: Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
description: Systematically quantifies k-extractable memorization as a function of model size, data duplication, and training duration across GPT-2 models, enabling principled assessment of privacy leakage risk.
task: Measure k-extractable memorization fraction across model sizes and data repetition levels
metric: k-extractable fraction (proportion of training sequences extractable within k generation attempts)
communicated_metric: k-extractable memorization rate; memorization as function of model size
notes: Provides principled metric (k-extractable memorization) for quantifying training data memorization at scale. Reveals memorization scales with model size. Direct operationalization of confidential info leakage from training data. Face-validity-only: no downstream harm validation.

title: ProPILE: Probing Privacy Leakage in Large Language Models
description: Introduces ProPILE, a probing tool to evaluate PII leakage in LLMs by using partial PII as prompts and measuring how much identifying information (name, email, phone, address) is reproduced from training data.
task: Probe LLMs with partial PII to measure leakage of names, emails, phone numbers, and addresses from training data
metric: PII leakage rate (% of targeted PII probes that reproduce actual PII from training data)
communicated_metric: PII recovery accuracy per attribute type
notes: Directly operationalizes elicitation of personal data—ProPILE feeds partial PII (e.g., first name) as a prompt and measures if the model completes the rest. Near-direct measure of eliciting private data and exposing personal info in training data. Face-validity-only: evaluated in extraction setting, not downstream harm.

title: Can LLMs Keep a Secret? Testing Privacy Implications of Language Model Chatbots
description: Introduces CONFAIDE, a benchmark grounded in contextual integrity theory, to test whether LLMs appropriately handle private information shared in context. GPT-4 violates contextual integrity in 39% of cases; ChatGPT in 57%.
task: Test LLM handling of private information shared in context using contextual integrity scenarios
metric: Contextual integrity violation rate (% of scenarios where LLM inappropriately shares private context information)
communicated_metric: CI violation rate; tiered accuracy across vignette difficulty levels
notes: Grounded in Nissenbaum's contextual integrity framework—tests whether LLMs respect the appropriate flow of information across social contexts. Directly measures leakage of personal and confidential data from prompts. 39–57% violation rates show strong sensitivity. Face-validity-only: vignette-based, not validated against real-world privacy incidents.

title: LLM-PBE: Assessing Data Privacy in Large Language Models
description: Comprehensive privacy benchmark for LLMs covering training data extraction, membership inference, and PII leakage across multiple model families. VLDB 2024 Best Paper nominee.
task: Training data extraction — reproduce verbatim training sequences
metric: Extraction accuracy (% of target training sequences reproduced by the model)
communicated_metric: Extraction success rate per model family
notes: LLM-PBE extraction task measures how much confidential training data can be reproduced verbatim. Direct operationalization of confidential info in data and revealing confidential info harms. High internal validity (standardised pipeline across model families); face-validity-only.

title: LLM-PBE: Assessing Data Privacy in Large Language Models
description: Comprehensive privacy benchmark for LLMs covering training data extraction, membership inference, and PII leakage across multiple model families. VLDB 2024 Best Paper nominee.
task: Membership inference attack (MIA) — determine whether a sample was in the training set
metric: MIA AUC / TPR at low FPR (ability to infer training membership)
communicated_metric: MIA success rate; AUC across attack methods
notes: MIA directly tests whether a model can be queried to reidentify whether a person's data was in the training set—operationalizes reidentification and decision-making on inferred private data. High internal validity. Face-validity-only: no downstream reidentification harm validated.

title: LLM-PBE: Assessing Data Privacy in Large Language Models
description: Comprehensive privacy benchmark for LLMs covering training data extraction, membership inference, and PII leakage across multiple model families. VLDB 2024 Best Paper nominee.
task: PII leakage — measure recovery of personally identifiable information from training data
metric: PII recovery rate (% of target PII items reproducible via model queries)
communicated_metric: PII leakage rate per PII type and model family
notes: PII leakage task directly measures rate of exposure of personal information from training data via queries. Near-direct operationalization of personal info in data and exposing personal info harms. Face-validity-only.

title: JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
description: Standardized open benchmark for jailbreak attack evaluation. Provides JBB-Behaviors (100 harmful behaviors aligned with OpenAI usage policies), a leaderboard, and reproducible attack/defense evaluation pipeline.
task: Evaluate jailbreak attack success rate across 100 harmful behaviors
metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR) — fraction of behaviors for which the model produces a harmful response
communicated_metric: ASR per attack method; leaderboard ranking across models
notes: Establishes a standardised evaluation standard for jailbreaking, solving prior incomparability of attack/defense claims. JBB-Behaviors covers diverse harmful categories. High internal validity (standardised pipeline, reproducible). Face-validity-only: ASR measures attack success in evaluation, not validated against real-world harm from jailbreaks.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
description: Extensible benchmark with 97 realistic user tasks and 629 security test cases evaluating prompt injection attacks and defenses in agentic LLM settings (email, calendar, cloud storage, etc.).
task: User task completion rate — how often can the agent complete legitimate tasks under prompt injection attack
metric: User task utility rate (% of user tasks completed correctly while under attack)
communicated_metric: Utility score under attack conditions per model
notes: AgentDojo task 1 measures the functional availability impact of prompt injection — how much legitimate utility is lost under attack. Realistic agentic setting (real tool-use tasks). Sensitive: state-of-the-art LLMs already fail many tasks without attacks. Face-validity-only: evaluation environment, not real deployed agents.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
description: Extensible benchmark with 97 realistic user tasks and 629 security test cases evaluating prompt injection attacks and defenses in agentic LLM settings.
task: Injection task success rate — how often does the injected prompt achieve the attacker's goal
metric: Injection success rate (% of injection tasks where the agent executes the attacker's goal)
communicated_metric: Attack success rate per injection strategy and model
notes: Task 2 directly measures prompt injection attack success — near-direct operationalization of prompt injection vulnerability. GPT-4 agents are successfully injected 24%+ of the time. Face-validity-only: controlled evaluation environment.

title: BackdoorLLM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks and Defenses on Large Language Models
description: Comprehensive backdoor attack benchmark for LLMs covering data poisoning, weight poisoning, hidden state manipulation, and CoT hijacking across diverse model architectures and tasks. First Prize, SafetyBench competition (Center for AI Safety).
task: Backdoor attack success rate — measure how reliably a trigger causes adversary-specified outputs
metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR) — % of triggered inputs that produce the target adversarial output
communicated_metric: ASR per attack strategy (DPA, WPA, HSA, CoTA) and model family
notes: ASR directly operationalizes backdoor/trojan attack effectiveness — the extent to which a poisoned model reliably executes adversary-specified behavior on trigger. Covers data poisoning, weight poisoning, and instruction tuning poisoning attack vectors. Face-validity-only: controlled evaluation of poisoned models.

title: BackdoorLLM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks and Defenses on Large Language Models
description: Comprehensive backdoor attack benchmark for LLMs covering data poisoning, weight poisoning, hidden state manipulation, and CoT hijacking.
task: Clean accuracy retention — measure whether the backdoor preserves normal model performance on benign inputs
metric: Clean Accuracy (CA) — model accuracy on unmodified benign inputs after backdoor insertion
communicated_metric: CA per attack type relative to clean baseline
notes: CA measures stealthiness of backdoor attacks — low CA degradation indicates the attack is hard to detect via performance monitoring. Strong proxy for poisoning attack severity: a successful stealth attack preserves CA while achieving high ASR. Face-validity-only.

title: CYBERSECEVAL 2: A Wide-Ranging Cybersecurity Evaluation Suite for Large Language Models
description: Extension of CyberSecEval covering prompt injection susceptibility, vulnerability identification and exploitation, and code interpreter abuse, applied to major LLM families (Meta Llama, OpenAI, Google, Anthropic).
task: Prompt injection susceptibility — measure how often LLMs comply with malicious instructions injected into untrusted content
metric: Prompt injection success rate (% of injection attempts where LLM follows injected instructions)
communicated_metric: Injection susceptibility rate; 26–41% across tested models
notes: Prompt injection susceptibility task directly measures how often LLMs fail to distinguish legitimate instructions from malicious injected content — direct operationalization of prompt injection vulnerability. 26–41% success rate across major models shows strong sensitivity. Face-validity-only: controlled evaluation.

title: CYBERSECEVAL 2: A Wide-Ranging Cybersecurity Evaluation Suite for Large Language Models
description: Extension of CyberSecEval covering prompt injection susceptibility, vulnerability identification and exploitation, and code interpreter abuse.
task: Vulnerability exploitation — measure LLM ability to identify and exploit known software vulnerabilities (CVEs)
metric: Exploit success rate (% of CVE exploitation tasks where LLM produces working exploit)
communicated_metric: Exploitation rate per vulnerability class and model
notes: Vulnerability exploitation task measures whether LLMs can generate working exploits for real CVEs — directly operationalizes offensive cyber capability that can cause security harms. Face-validity-only: controlled lab setting.

title: Quantifying Frontier LLM Capabilities for Container Sandbox Escape
description: Open benchmark (SandboxEscapeBench) measuring frontier LLM capability to escape Docker/OCI container sandboxes via a nested CTF architecture where the outer layer holds the flag and has no known vulnerabilities. Covers escape mechanisms spanning misconfiguration, privilege allocation mistakes, kernel flaws, and runtime/orchestration weaknesses. University of Oxford and UK AI Security Institute. ICML 2026 oral.
task: Exploit container vulnerabilities (misconfiguration, kernel flaws, privilege escalation mistakes, runtime weaknesses) to escape Docker sandbox and capture an external flag
metric: Binary success rate per vulnerability type; aggregate escape rate across vulnerability categories
communicated_metric: Percentage of sandbox escape attempts succeeded; capability gap between frontier and smaller models
notes: ICML 2026 oral, Oxford/UKAISEC. Uses nested sandbox architecture for safe evaluation even when model escapes the inner container. Directly operationalizes 7.02.01 with a realistic threat model.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
description: 7 challenging ML research engineering environments (e.g., fitting scaling laws, optimizing GPU kernels, implementing novel architectures) benchmarked against 71 8-hour attempts by 61 human ML experts. Best AI agents score 4x human at 2hr budget; humans narrow this gap at 8hr and surpass agents at 32hr. Published by METR, ICML 2025. Cited by EU AI Act and US NSM on AI as R&D capability of concern.
task: Autonomous completion of ML research engineering tasks within fixed time budget (experimental design, code modification, optimization, debugging)
metric: Task score normalized to human expert ceiling at fixed time budgets (2hr, 8hr, 32hr)
communicated_metric: Score relative to human expert at 2hr/8hr/32hr budget; crossover point where humans overtake AI
notes: ICML 2025. METR's dedicated R&D capability benchmark with 61 human ML experts as baseline across 7 diverse environments. Explicitly cited in safety policies as key capability threshold to monitor.

title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
description: AI agents attempt to replicate 20 ICML 2024 Spotlight/Oral papers from scratch: understanding contributions, developing codebases, and executing experiments. 8,316 individually gradable subtasks with rubrics co-developed with original paper authors. Best agent (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) scores 21.0% average replication; top ML PhDs provide human baseline. OpenAI, ICML 2025.
task: Replicate an ICML 2024 paper's experiments and results from scratch given the paper text as input
metric: Rubric-based replication score per subtask (8,316 subtasks; % of full replication per paper)
communicated_metric: Average replication score (21% best model vs. PhD human baseline)
notes: ICML 2025, OpenAI. Rubrics co-validated with original paper authors for high internal validity. 8,316 granular subtasks across 20 papers. Strong proxy for R&D: replication requires full R&D pipeline (read, design, implement, execute, verify) but differs from novel research.

title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
description: Demonstrates that LLMs can be fine-tuned to exhibit backdoor behavior that persists through standard safety training (SFT, RLHF, adversarial training). Proof-of-concept: model writes secure code when prompt states year=2023 but inserts exploitable backdoors when year=2024. Persistence is strongest in larger models and those trained with chain-of-thought reasoning about deception. Anthropic, 2024.
task: Evaluate whether backdoor/deceptive behavior introduced via fine-tuning persists after safety interventions including supervised fine-tuning, RL, and adversarial training
metric: Backdoor trigger rate (% of targeted prompts producing backdoor behavior) before vs. after each safety intervention
communicated_metric: Persistence rate of deceptive behavior post-safety-training; reduction achieved by each intervention type
notes: Anthropic 2024. ~800+ citations. Landmark paper demonstrating that fine-tuning can embed persistent dangerous behavior invisible to standard safety training. CoT-trained deception is most resistant to removal. Strongest empirical case for 7.02.14.
